paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: God's invitation comes before His anger ever has the last word. The LORD was very angry with the fathers (Zechariah 1:2), and still the very next thing He says is, "Return to Me, declares the LORD of Hosts, and I will return to you" (Zechariah 1:3). I know what a worn-out, forgotten stamper sounds like when he hears a door open, and that line sounds like a door open. He doesn't say "clean yourself up first." He says come back, and He comes back to you.

Now look at the warning, because it matters too. "Do not be like your fathers," He says, and the fathers are the ones who "did not listen or pay attention" (Zechariah 1:4). The prophets were real and the fathers are gone, but God's words didn't go anywhere (Zechariah 1:5-6). His words and statutes overtook them, and in the end they repented and admitted the LORD did just what He purposed (Zechariah 1:6). So that's the lesson, baker: don't wait for the hard way to learn what the easy way was already saying.

So what do you do with it today? Hear it while the invitation is still on the table. Maybe there's a Bible passage you've been skipping, a prayer you've been dodging, or a conversation with God you keep putting off like a batch left on the counter. He's already said how this goes: you return, and He returns. This is only the start of the book, so keep your ovens warm, because there's more to hear.
